Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay a colorful mat on a flat floor. 2. Place the child on their belly. 3. Put a mirror or high-contrast toy in front of them to encourage neck lifting.
1. Lay the child on their back. 2. Shake a rattle to one side of their head. 3. Move the rattle slowly toward the floor to guide their body to roll over to reach it.
1. Sit the child on a firm surface. 2. Place supportive pillows around their back and sides. 3. Place a toy in front of them to encourage staying upright.
1. Get into a crawling position with the child. 2. Roll a ball just out of their reach. 3. Cheer as they move forward to "catch" the ball.
1. Place a toy at the far end of a sturdy sofa. 2. Help the child stand and hold the furniture. 3. Encourage side-steps toward the toy.
1. Position the child behind a stable walker. 2. Assist their grip on the handle. 3. Encourage them to push it forward toward you.
1. Place a soft ball in front of the child's feet. 2. Demonstrate a kicking motion. 3. Hold their hand for balance as they try to swing their leg at the ball.
1. Place a strip of colored tape on the floor. 2. Hold the child's hands. 3. Guide them to walk one foot in front of the other along the line.
1. Stack several firm sofa cushions on a carpeted floor. 2. Place a toy on top of the stack. 3. Help the child crawl up the cushions to retrieve it.
1. Stand on a flat, soft surface. 2. Hold the child’s hands for support. 3. Count "1, 2, 3, Jump!" and encourage them to bend their knees and hop off the floor.
1. Place a toy two steps up on a staircase. 2. Support the child at the hips. 3. Encourage them to reach for the next step and pull their knees up.
1. Set up a play tunnel or a row of open boxes. 2. Sit at the far end and call the child’s name. 3. Encourage them to crawl through the dark space to find you.
1. Play upbeat music with a clear rhythm. 2. Hold the child's hands and bounce or sway. 3. Encourage them to spin, clap, or wiggle their hips to the beat.
1. Stand a short distance from the child. 2. Demonstrate an overhand or underhand throw with a soft ball. 3. Encourage them to throw the ball toward a target like a basket.
1. Arrange pillows and toys in a path. 2. Guide the child by the hand through the path. 3. Encourage them to step over the pillows and weave through the toys.
1. Call out an animal (e.g., "Bear"). 2. Show the child how to crawl on hands and feet like a bear. 3. Change to a "Frog" and show them how to squat and hop.
1. Place your hands on top of your head like ears. 2. Demonstrate short, quick hops. 3. Encourage the child to follow you around the room hopping on both feet.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child jumping with hands on head]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Play a rhythmic "marching" song. 2. Encourage the child to lift their knees high with each step. 3. Swing your arms in sync with your legs to show the motion.
1. Stand a few feet away from the child. 2. Gently roll a ball toward their feet. 3. Encourage them to wait for the ball and kick it back to you as it arrives.
1. Walk around the room performing an action (e.g., clapping). 2. Tell the child to "Do what I do!". 3. Change the action to something else, like touching your nose or hopping.

1. Place 4-5 firm pillows in a straight or curved line on a carpeted floor. 2. Hold the child's hands as they step from one pillow to the next. 3. Encourage them to maintain balance on the uneven surface until they reach the end.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child stepping on a pillow path]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Stand at one end of a clear room. 2. Tell the child to run toward you when you say "Go!". 3. Shout "Stop!" and show them how to freeze in place, then repeat the cycle.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child freezing in a running pose]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a weighted laundry basket or a large toy box on a smooth floor. 2. Show the child how to place both hands on the side. 3. Encourage them to use their legs to push the object across the room to a "finish line."

1. Place several low objects (like pool noodles or rolled towels) on the floor. 2. Lead the child toward the obstacles. 3. Encourage them to lift one leg high to step over without touching the object.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child lifting leg over a towel]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Gently toss a bright balloon into the air. 2. Encourage the child to look up and follow its movement. 3. Have them run or reach out to tap the balloon to keep it from hitting the ground.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child reaching for a floating balloon]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Blow several bubbles toward the floor. 2. Point to the bubbles as they land. 3. Encourage the child to run and "stomp" on the bubbles with their feet to pop them.
1. Set up "hurdles" using small blocks with a stick across them. 2. Hold the child's hand for support. 3. Guide them to step over each hurdle carefully, focusing on lifting their knees.
Tools (Column E): Toy blocks and a wooden dowel
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child stepping over a small hurdle]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Tell the child you are "sneaking" like a quiet mouse. 2. Demonstrate walking on the balls of your feet with heels lifted. 3. Encourage them to follow you quietly across the room on their tiptoes.
1. Stand facing the child and hold their hands. 2. Take a slow step backward and pull them gently toward you. 3. Encourage them to look over their shoulder and take small steps in reverse.
1. Give the child a medium-sized playground ball. 2. Show them how to push the ball forward with two hands while walking. 3. Encourage them to keep the ball moving in a straight line toward a target.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pushing a ball while walking]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a rattle in the child's open palm. 2. Gently close their fingers around the handle. 3. Encourage them to shake the rattle to hear the sound, reinforcing their grip strength.
1. Sit with the child and a set of large blocks. 2. Place one block down and stack another on top. 3. Hand a block to the child and gesture for them to add it to the tower.

1. Provide a large plastic cup and several small safe objects (like large pom-poms). 2. Show the child how to pick up one object at a time. 3. Encourage them to drop the object into the cup and listen for the "plink."
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child dropping a ball into a cup]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place an empty bowl and a bowl filled with dry cereal side-by-side. 2. Give the child a chunky spoon. 3. Help them scoop the cereal and move it into the empty bowl.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child moving items with a spoon]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use an extra-thick lace or a stiff pipe cleaner. 2. Hold a large bead with a wide hole. 3. Guide the child to push the lace through the hole and pull it out the other side.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child threading a bead onto a string]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Partially peel the edge of a large sticker from a sheet. 2. Show the child how to pinch the edge with their thumb and forefinger. 3. Encourage them to pull the sticker off and press it onto a piece of paper.

1. Give the child a golf-ball-sized piece of soft playdough. 2. Show them how to squeeze it tight in their fist so it oozes through their fingers. 3. Encourage them to poke it, squish it, and pull it apart.

1. Tape a large piece of paper to the table to prevent sliding. 2. Give the child a thick "egg" or triangular crayon. 3. Demonstrate making a mark and encourage them to move their arm to make their own lines.
1. Use a jar with a slot cut into the lid. 2. Give the child large buttons (too big to swallow). 3. Show them how to orient the button vertically to fit it through the slot.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child putting button in a jar slot]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a strip of colorful tissue paper or thin construction paper. 2. Demonstrate holding the paper with both hands and pulling in opposite directions. 3. Encourage them to tear the paper into many small pieces.
1. Clip several clothespins to the rim of a sturdy bowl. 2. Show the child how to squeeze the peg to open the "mouth." 3. Encourage them to pull the pegs off one by one and drop them into the bowl.
1. Remove one piece from a large wooden knob puzzle. 2. Hand the piece to the child and point to the empty space. 3. Guide their hand to rotate and drop the piece into the matching slot.
1. Place a dollop of non-toxic paint on a large sheet of paper. 2. Show the child how to dip one finger into the paint. 3. Encourage them to smear, swirl, and make dots across the paper surface.
1. Use a plastic piggy bank or a container with a thin slit. 2. Give the child large plastic play coins. 3. Show them how to line up the coin with the slot and push it all the way in.
1. Draw a large, bold circle or square on a piece of paper. 2. Have the child dip their finger in water or paint. 3. Guide their finger to follow the lines of the shape from start to finish.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Paper with a large red circle]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Poke several holes in the bottom of an upside-down colander. 2. Give the child colorful pipe cleaners. 3. Show them how to poke the end of the pipe cleaner into a hole and push it through.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child poking wire into a hole]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a mix of two different items (e.g., large pasta and blocks) in a pile. 2. Provide two separate containers. 3. Show the child how to pick up a block and put it in one container, then pasta in the other.
1. Set out a set of graduated stacking cups. 2. Show the child how to place the largest cup down first. 3. Encourage them to find the next size and stack it precisely on top to build a tower.

1. Stick several short strips of painter's tape to a high-chair tray or table. 2. Peel up one corner of each strip. 3. Encourage the child to use their "pincer grasp" to grab the corner and pull the tape off.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pulling tape off a table]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Provide several small plastic containers with different types of lids (flip, pull, or screw). 2. Hide a small toy inside one. 3. Show the child how to remove the lid to find the toy, then help them put it back on.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pulling a lid off a tub]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Scatter soft pom-poms on a flat surface. 2. Give the child a pair of large plastic tweezers or tongs. 3. Show them how to squeeze the tongs to grab a pom-pom and move it to a basket.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child using tongs on a ball]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use toys or straps that have Velcro fasteners. 2. Close the Velcro firmly. 3. Encourage the child to grab the edge of the strap and pull hard to hear the "rrip" sound as it opens.
1. Use a wooden board with large, secure pegs (Geoboard). 2. Show the child how to hook a thick rubber band onto one peg. 3. Encourage them to pull and stretch the band to hook it onto a second peg.
1. Place a pegboard in front of the child. 2. Hand them one large plastic peg. 3. Point to a hole and guide them to push the peg down until it stays upright in the board.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child inserting a peg into a board]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place one bowl filled with water and one empty bowl. 2. Put a small sponge in the water bowl. 3. Show the child how to move the wet sponge to the empty bowl and squeeze hard to release the water.
1. Use a "pop-up" toy or an activity center with buttons. 2. Point to a specific button. 3. Show the child how to use their pointer finger to push the button down to trigger a sound or a pop-up.
1. Sit with the child and a sturdy board book. 2. Show them how to slide their finger under the edge of the page. 3. Encourage them to turn one page at a time to see the next picture.
1. Remove all rings from a stacking post. 2. Hand the largest ring to the child. 3. Point to the post and encourage them to drop the ring over the top so it slides to the bottom.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a ring on a post]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a sheet of newspaper or thin wrapping paper. 2. Show them how to use both hands to crush the paper into a small ball. 3. Encourage them to throw the "paper ball" into a basket.
1. Provide a large toy nut and bolt set. 2. Hold the bolt steady for the child. 3. Show them how to twist the nut with their fingers to move it up or down the screw thread.

1. Sit at eye level with the child so they can see your mouth clearly. 2. Speak slowly using exaggerated facial expressions and lip movements. 3. Pause frequently to give the child a chance to respond with a sound or facial movement.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent at eye-level talking to baby]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Listen for a sound the child makes naturally (e.g., "ba"). 2. Repeat the exact sound back to them immediately. 3. Wait for them to make the sound again, creating a back-and-forth "conversation" of babbles.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent leaning in to listen to baby]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hold a familiar object like a "Ball" clearly in front of the child. 2. Say the name of the object twice: "Ball... Ball." 3. Encourage the child to look at the object and try to repeat the name or point to it.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent holding a shoe and naming it]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Show the child a picture of a common animal (e.g., a cow). 2. Make the animal's sound clearly ("Moo!"). 3. Encourage the child to copy the sound whenever you point to that animal's picture.
Tools (Column E): Animal picture book or toy animals
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child making a "moo" face with toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Open a book with large, simple pictures. 2. Instead of reading the story, point to a picture and describe it: "Look at the big blue bird!" 3. Ask the child "Where is the bird?" and guide their hand to point to it.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child looking at a book]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. When the child wants something, use two-word phrases to describe it (e.g., "More juice" or "Blue ball"). 2. Encourage the child to attempt a second word by pausing after the first: "Want... [pause]... cookie?". 3. Celebrate any vocal attempt they make.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent holding a toy out to a child]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a toy phone and take one for yourself. 2. Hold the phone to your ear and say "Hello? Is [Child's Name] there?". 3. Hand the phone to them and encourage them to "talk" and listen into the receiver.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child holding toy phone to ear]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Sing a short, simple song like "Twinkle Twinkle" several times. 2. Use the same hand gestures every time you sing it. 3. Eventually, stop singing at the end of a line (e.g., "How I wonder what you...") and wait for the child to fill in the last word.
1. Point to your own nose and say "Nose." 2. Gently touch the child's nose and say "Your nose!". 3. Ask "Where is your nose?" and encourage them to point to their own or yours.
1. Perform a simple action like "Jump" or "Clap." 2. Say the word as you do the action: "I am jumping!". 3. Encourage the child to do the same and say the word along with you.

1. Ask simple "Yes/No" questions throughout the day (e.g., "Do you want water?"). 2. Exaggerate a nod for "Yes" and a shake for "No." 3. Wait for the child to respond with a gesture or a sound before providing the item.

1. Say two words that rhyme clearly (e.g., "Cat, Hat"). 2. Repeat them with an emphasis on the ending sound. 3. Say a short rhyme and clap your hands on the rhyming words to draw the child's attention to the sound pattern.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Card with a cat and a hat]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Read a very familiar story to the child. 2. Turn to a page and ask "What happened here?". 3. Encourage the child to use one or two words to describe the picture or what comes next in the story.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pointing at a book page]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Make a very happy face and say "I am happy!". 2. Use a mirror so the child can see their own face. 3. Ask them to "Make a happy face" and name the emotion they are showing.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child looking in mirror making a face]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a desired toy slightly out of reach but in plain sight. 2. Wait for the child to gesture or make a sound. 3. Prompt them by saying "What do you want?" and encourage them to use a word or point clearly before giving it to them.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child reaching and vocalizing for toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Put three different toys in front of the child (e.g., car, doll, ball). 2. Ask "Where is the car?". 3. Encourage the child to point to or pick up the correct toy, then say the name of the toy together.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: A car, a doll, and a ball]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child picking up a specific toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Say a simple, fun word like "Pop!" or "Boom!". 2. Encourage the child to "echo" or repeat the word back to you. 3. Make it a game by changing the volume from a whisper to a loud voice and having them match you.

1. Sing a rhyme that has specific motions (e.g., "Itsy Bitsy Spider"). 2. Guide the child's hands to perform the movements as you sing. 3. Pause during the song to see if the child will start the next hand motion on their own.

1. Hold up two different items (e.g., an apple and a banana). 2. Ask "Do you want the apple or the banana?". 3. Wait for the child to look at or point to their choice, then repeat the name of the chosen item clearly.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pointing to one of two items]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Show a busy picture with many items (like a park scene). 2. Say "Find the doggie!". 3. Encourage the child to scan the picture and point to the correct object, then reward them with praise.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pointing to a detail in a book]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Pick up a toy and point to a specific feature (e.g., "The car is red"). 2. Use simple sensory words like "soft," "loud," or "shiny" to describe it. 3. Encourage the child to touch the toy while you repeat the descriptive word.

1. Hide behind a chair or door with an object that makes a distinct noise (like a bell). 2. Make the sound and ask, "What was that?". 3. Reveal the object, name it, and let the child make the sound themselves.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child listening intently to a sound]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Look through a photo album or digital pictures of family members. 2. Point to a person and ask "Who is that?". 3. Say the name (e.g., "Grandpa") and encourage the child to repeat it or wave at the picture.
1. Place a toy in an obvious but slightly hidden spot (e.g., under a clear cloth). 2. Ask the child, "Where is your teddy?". 3. Encourage them to look around and point to or crawl toward the object.

1. Say a simple, silly sound or a word (e.g., "Beep-beep!"). 2. Look at the child expectantly and wait for them to try and mimic you. 3. Gradually increase the difficulty to two-word phrases once they master single sounds.

1. Sing a very familiar nursery rhyme with a strong rhythm. 2. Stop abruptly before a rhyming word or a key phrase (e.g., "The wheels on the bus go round and..."). 3. Wait for the child to finish the line with a sound, word, or gesture.

1. Narrate what you are doing during a daily task like diapering or dressing. 2. Use simple sentences: "Now we put on your sock. One sock, two socks." 3. Pause to see if the child anticipates the next step by looking or moving.

1. Walk around the house and listen for specific sounds (a ticking clock, a bird, a running tap). 2. Point to your ear and say "Listen! I hear a..." 3. Lead the child to the source of the sound and name the object making it.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child with hand to ear listening]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. When the child says a single word (e.g., "Dog"), repeat it back and add a word. 2. Say, "Yes, big dog!" or "Brown dog!". 3. This helps the child learn how to combine words into short phrases.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent nodding and talking to child]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Sit with the child in front of a large mirror. 2. Make funny faces or stick out your tongue and describe the action. 3. Encourage the child to "talk" to their reflection and watch how their mouth moves.

1. Hold a black-and-white high-contrast card about 8-12 inches from the infant's face. 2. Slowly move the card from side to side. 3. Watch as the child tracks the bold patterns, which helps develop visual focus and brain connections.
1. Hide your face behind your hands or a scarf. 2. Ask "Where is Mama/Papa?" in an excited voice. 3. Quickly reveal your face and say "Peekaboo!" to teach that things exist even when unseen.

1. Show the child a toy, then hide it completely under a small blanket while they watch. 2. Ask "Where did it go?". 3. Encourage the child to lift the blanket to find the toy, building memory and persistence.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child lifting a blanket to find toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Present a shape sorter with only one type of hole open (e.g., the circle). 2. Hand the child the matching shape. 3. Guide their hand to align the shape and push it through the hole.
1. Use two bowls of different colors (e.g., Red and Blue). 2. Provide several red and blue blocks. 3. Show the child how to "match" the red block to the red bowl, then encourage them to try.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing block in matching bowl]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a puzzle with only 2 or 3 large pieces. 2. Remove the pieces and show the child the empty board. 3. Encourage them to fit the pieces back by matching the shapes and pictures.
1. Lay out two pairs of identical cards face up. 2. Point to one and ask the child to "find the one just like this." 3. Encourage them to pick up the matching card, reinforcing visual memory.

1. Use nesting cups or rings of different sizes. 2. Show the child that the small one fits inside the big one. 3. Encourage them to experiment with the order to see which ones fit together and which ones don't.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child trying to fit cups together]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Present a toy that reacts to an action (e.g., a jack-in-the-box or a button that makes a light flash). 2. Demonstrate the action clearly. 3. Encourage the child to repeat the action to get the same fun result.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pressing a button for light]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Safely hold the child near a light switch. 2. Say "Lights ON" as you flip it up, and "Lights OFF" as you flip it down. 3. Let the child try to move the switch themselves to see the immediate change in the room.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent holding child to reach switch]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Fill a basket with various items like blocks, socks, and spoons. 2. Set out three empty containers. 3. Show the child how to put all the blocks in one, socks in the second, and spoons in the third.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child sorting items into three bins]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place two different colored blocks in a row (e.g., Red, Blue). 2. Hand the child a red block and a blue block. 3. Encourage them to place their blocks in the same order next to yours.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Red and blue blocks in a line]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Line up 3-5 large items like toy cars. 2. Touch each item one by one as you say the number clearly: "One, two, three..." 3. Encourage the child to touch the items along with you as you count.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Five toy cars in a row]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Finger touching a toy while counting]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay out three different picture cards (e.g., Apple, Dog, Sun). 2. Hand the child a duplicate "Apple" card. 3. Ask them to "Find the one that looks like this" and place it on top of the matching card.

1. Hide a noisy toy (like a ticking timer or music box) under a pillow. 2. Ask the child "Where is the music coming from?". 3. Encourage them to follow the sound and lift the pillow to reveal the "treasure".
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child listening for a hidden toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Scatter several toys of different colors on the floor. 2. Ask the child "Can you find something red?". 3. Praise them when they pick up a red item and name the color again to reinforce the concept.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child holding up a red toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Build a tall tower of soft blocks in front of the child. 2. Say "1, 2, 3... Knock it down!". 3. Let the child push the tower over, then encourage them to help you rebuild it to learn cause and effect.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pushing over a block tower]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Mix toy animals and toy vehicles in a pile. 2. Label two boxes: "Animals" and "Cars." 3. Show the child how to sort them, explaining that one group has legs and the other has wheels.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Toy cow and toy truck side-by-side]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a cow in an animal bin]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child 5 blocks and keep 5 for yourself. 2. Tell them "Let's see how high we can go!". 3. Take turns adding one block at a time to a single tower, teaching patience and steady hand movements.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child adding to a tower]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place three familiar toys on a tray (e.g., Ball, Cup, Spoon). 2. Have the child close their eyes, then remove one toy. 3. Ask "What is gone?" and encourage them to remember the missing item.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child looking at a tray with one empty spot]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Draw the outlines (shadows) of 3 simple toys on a piece of paper. 2. Hand the child the actual toys. 3. Encourage them to place each toy onto its corresponding "shadow" drawing.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a toy on its outline]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Provide a large empty bucket and a scoop of dry rice or sand. 2. Show the child how to fill the bucket to the top. 3. Then, show them how to pour it all out to understand concepts of "full" and "empty".
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pouring rice from a scoop]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hold up a large ball and a very small ball. 2. Ask the child "Which one is BIG?". 3. Encourage them to point to or grab the larger object, then repeat the word "Big".
Tools (Column E): One large ball, one small ball
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Large beach ball and small tennis ball]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pointing to a large object]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay out a sequence of activities (e.g., Brush hair, then put on hat). 2. Show the child the two steps in order. 3. Ask them "What do we do first?" and guide them through the simple two-step routine.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child brushing hair then reaching for hat]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a small toy under one of two identical cups while the child watches. 2. Slowly move the cups around. 3. Ask "Where is the toy?" and let the child lift a cup to find it.
Tools (Column E): Two identical plastic cups, small toy
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child lifting a cup to find a toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Clap a simple rhythm (e.g., Clap-Clap, Pause). 2. Look at the child and say "Your turn!". 3. Encourage them to mimic the same rhythm, helping them develop auditory memory.

1. Stand behind the child and make a sound (e.g., shake a bell or crinkle paper). 2. Ask "Where is that sound?". 3. Encourage the child to turn their head or point in the direction the sound came from.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child turning head toward a sound]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give a simple command with two parts: "Pick up the ball and put it in the box." 2. Wait for the child to process both steps. 3. Praise them for completing the sequence in the correct order.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a ball into a box]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Scatter 3 pairs of identical socks on the floor. 2. Pick up one sock and show it to the child. 3. Ask "Can you find the other one just like this?" to encourage visual matching.

1. Draw a wide, simple path on a piece of paper leading from a "Start" to a "Finish" (e.g., a mouse to a cheese). 2. Show the child how to move their finger along the path. 3. Encourage them to stay "inside the lines" until the end.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child tracing a line with their finger]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Sit with the child in front of a mirror. 2. Make a big, bright smile and say "Happy!". 3. Wait for the child to see your reflection and encourage them to smile back at themselves and you.
1. Sit facing the child and start a slow, rhythmic clap. 2. Reach out and gently help the child clap their hands together. 3. Cheer and laugh together to celebrate the shared rhythmic movement.
1. Sit on the floor across from the child. 2. Roll a soft ball to them and say "Your turn!". 3. Wait for them to roll it back and say "My turn!", teaching the flow of social play.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child rolling a ball]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a doll or teddy bear and a toy spoon. 2. Show them how to "feed" the doll. 3. Encourage the child to mimic the nurturing action, fostering early empathy.
1. Play with a set of blocks together. 2. Hand a block to the child and say "One for you." 3. Ask the child to "Give one to me," praising them when they hand a toy over.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child handing a toy to a parent]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Sit in a circle with family or other children. 2. Sing a familiar song with hand motions like "If You're Happy and You Know It." 3. Encourage the child to look at others and join in the collective movements.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Children sitting in a circle singing]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Make an exaggerated face (Happy, Sad, Surprised). 2. Name the emotion clearly: "I am sad." 3. Ask the child to copy your face and name the feeling together.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child making funny faces]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. When someone leaves the room, say "Bye-bye!". 2. Demonstrate a waving motion with your hand. 3. Help the child lift their hand and wave to practice social greetings and departures.
1. Open your arms wide and say "Hug?". 2. Lean in for a gentle embrace. 3. Encourage the child to initiate hugs with you or a favorite stuffed animal to express affection.
1. Sit behind or to the side of the child while they play. 2. Call their name clearly in a cheerful voice. 3. Reward them with a smile or a tickle the moment they turn their head to acknowledge you.
1. Provide a toy pot and a wooden spoon. 2. Show the child how to "stir" the pot. 3. Pretend to taste the "food" and say "Mmm, yummy!" to encourage imaginative role-play.
1. Set out a basket of easy-to-wear items like large hats or scarves. 2. Put a hat on yourself, then on the child. 3. Look in the mirror together and talk about the "new" characters you've become.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child wearing a large adult hat]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Say "I'm gonna get you!" in a playful tone. 2. Gently tickle the child's tummy or toes. 3. Pause and wait for their laughter or a "more" gesture before continuing to build social anticipation.
1. When a family member enters, say "Hello!". 2. Encourage the child to look at the person. 3. Prompt the child to wave or say a sound to acknowledge the arrival of a loved one.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child reaching for a person entering]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Read a book where a character is feeling an emotion. 2. Point to the character's face and say, "He is happy because he has a ball." 3. Ask the child "Are you happy?" to bridge the story to their own feelings.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child discussing a book]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hand a toy to the child and say "Here you go." 2. When the child hands you something, say "Thank you" with a big smile. 3. Model the behavior consistently to help the child learn the social rhythm of gratitude.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent smiling while receiving a toy]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hold your palm up and say "High Five!". 2. Guide the child's hand to slap yours. 3. Celebrate the contact with a cheer to build a sense of shared accomplishment.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child giving parent a high five]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hold a toy and offer it to the child. 2. Once they take it, gently ask "Can I have it please?". 3. When they give it back, praise them immediately to encourage the flow of reciprocal play.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child handing a toy back to parent]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Show the child a photo of a family member who isn't present. 2. Name the person and talk about them: "That's Grandma! She loves you." 3. Encourage the child to kiss the photo or wave to foster long-distance bonding.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child looking at a family photo]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay a teddy bear down and cover it with a small cloth. 2. Whisper "Shh, teddy is sleeping." 3. Have the child "pat" the bear gently to practice being quiet and careful with others.
1. When someone enters the room, say "Hello!" in a cheerful voice. 2. Demonstrate a waving motion. 3. Encourage the child to look at the person and mirror your wave to practice social greetings.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child waving at an open door]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Play a favorite upbeat song. 2. Hold the child's hands and bounce or sway together. 3. Laugh and cheer as you move, showing the child how to express joy through physical movement.
1. Identify a specific soft toy the child gravitates toward when tired or upset. 2. Offer the toy during quiet transitions or naps. 3. Use the toy to model self-soothing by hugging it yourself first.
1. Make a funny sound or a silly face (e.g., a "pop" sound with your cheek). 2. Wait for the child to react. 3. Repeat the action that made them laugh to build a shared sense of humor and connection.
1. Hold a large but lightweight toy (like a beach ball). 2. Ask the child "Can you help me?". 3. Have them hold one side while you hold the other as you move it across the room.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and child carrying a box]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Set out a few toy food items and a small basket. 2. Pretend to pick an item and put it in the basket. 3. Encourage the child to "shop" and hand you items to "buy," practicing social exchange.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing toy food in basket]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a toy stethoscope to "listen" to a teddy bear's heart. 2. Gently show the child how to do the same. 3. This reduces anxiety about real check-ups and encourages nurturing behavior.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child using toy on a teddy bear]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a few small crackers on a plate. 2. Take one and say "One for me." 3. Hand one to the child and say "One for you," teaching the basics of fair distribution and sharing.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child and parent sharing a snack]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use two dolls to act out a simple interaction, like waving "Hi." 2. Give one doll to the child and keep one for yourself. 3. Encourage the dolls to "talk" or play together to model friendship.

1. Lean close to the child and wait for them to look at you. 2. Give a big, warm smile and wait silently. 3. When they smile back, respond with a verbal "I see that big smile!" to reinforce emotional bonding.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent and baby smiling at each other]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a small amount of baby-safe oil or lotion. 2. Gently stroke the child's arms and legs with firm but soft pressure. 3. Narrate the touch (e.g., "Soft touch on your toes") to help them process tactile input.

1. Fill a low basket with items like silk, a loofah, a smooth stone, and a pinecone. 2. Encourage the child to reach in and explore. 3. Use words like "rough," "smooth," or "fuzzy" as they touch each item.
1. Fill a shallow tray with an inch of water. 2. Show the child how to tap the surface to make a splash. 3. Add a few floating toys to encourage them to reach and move their hands through the water.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child splashing water in a tub]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Fill a large plastic bin with dry rice. 2. Bury several small plastic toys under the rice. 3. Encourage the child to use their hands to "dig" through the rice and find the hidden treasures.
Tools (Column E): Large bin, dry rice, small toys

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Provide a small tray of clean play sand. 2. Show the child how to run their fingers through it or squeeze it. 3. Use a small rake or cup to show how the sand moves and takes shape.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pouring sand from a cup]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Roll out a flat "pancake" of playdough. 2. Give the child items like shells or large buttons. 3. Show them how to press the items into the dough to leave an impression, then peel them off.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pressing a hand into dough]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Blow a few bubbles into the air toward the child. 2. Encourage them to watch the bubbles move and track them with their eyes. 3. Show them how to reach out and "catch" a bubble on their hand before it pops.

1. Use a large, soft craft feather. 2. Gently brush the feather against the child's palm, arm, or cheek. 3. Observe their reaction to the light, ticklish sensation and name the feeling ("That's soft!").
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent brushing a feather on child's hand]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a few large ice cubes in a bowl. 2. Let the child touch the ice for a few seconds. 3. Talk about the sensation of "Cold!" and watch how the ice slips and melts in their hand.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Clear ice cubes in a bowl]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child touching a cold ice cube]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Provide two plastic cups, one filled with water. 2. Show the child how to pour water from one cup into the other. 3. Listen to the "glug-glug" sound and watch the water move to build hand-eye coordination.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child pouring water into a tray]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay out different "floor stations" using a rug, a towel, and bubble wrap. 2. Hold the child's hands as they walk barefoot over each surface. 3. Describe the change in feeling, such as "soft," "bumpy," or "scratchy."

1. Fill three identical plastic eggs with different items (beans, rice, a bell). 2. Shake one egg and listen to the unique sound it makes. 3. Encourage the child to shake the eggs and find the one that sounds "loud" or "quiet."

1. Dim the lights and shine a flashlight against a plain wall. 2. Move your hand in front of the light to create shadows. 3. Encourage the child to try and "catch" the shadow on the wall with their hands.

1. Hold a safe, scented item like a lemon slice or a cinnamon stick near the child. 2. Say "Mmm, smell the lemon!" and take a deep breath. 3. Observe the child's reaction as they take a sniff of the new scent.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child smelling a piece of fruit]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Turn on a small electric fan on a low setting. 2. Hold a lightweight scarf in front of the fan so it flutters. 3. Let the child feel the air on their skin and watch how the wind moves the fabric.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child feeling air from a fan]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Prepare a bowl of comfortably warm water (test on your wrist first). 2. Let the child dip their hands or feet into the water. 3. Talk about the "warm" sensation compared to the cool air in the room.

1. Place a metal spoon in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. 2. Gently touch the back of the cold spoon to the child’s palm or cheek. 3. Watch for their reaction to the sudden temperature change and say "Ooh, cold!".
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Parent touching spoon to child's hand]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Spray a small amount of unscented shaving foam or whipped cream onto a tray. 2. Show the child how to draw lines or circles in the foam with their finger. 3. Encourage them to squish the foam between their hands to feel the airy texture.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child drawing in foam on a tray]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Spread a thin layer of sand over a dark-colored tray. 2. Use your finger to draw a simple shape or a letter. 3. Have the child "erase" the drawing by shaking the tray and then let them draw their own lines.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Tray with a layer of sand]
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Finger drawing a circle in sand]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Collect several leaves of different shapes and textures (crunchy, smooth, fuzzy). 2. Let the child hold and crumble a dry leaf to hear the sound. 3. Compare it to a smooth green leaf to explore natural textures.
1. Take the child to a patch of clean, safe grass. 2. Let them stand or crawl barefoot on the grass. 3. Describe the feeling of the "tickly" grass on their skin as they move around.

1. Blow bubbles upward so they float down toward the child. 2. Encourage the child to use their "pointer finger" to poke a bubble. 3. Celebrate with a "Pop!" sound every time they successfully touch one.

1. Gather scraps of different fabrics like corduroy, satin, and fleece. 2. Rub a piece gently against the child's arm. 3. Let them grab the fabric and feel the difference between the "bumpy" and "soft" materials.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child feeling a piece of satin]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a sponge or a washcloth soaked in water. 2. Hold it above a bowl and squeeze it slowly so the water drips. 3. Encourage the child to watch the drops fall and listen to the "plop" sound in the water.

1. Use a ball with a unique texture (e.g., a nubby sensory ball). 2. Roll the ball slowly over the child's legs or back. 3. Encourage them to catch the ball and explore the "bumps" with their own hands.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Ball being rolled on child's arm]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a toy that gently vibrates when a string is pulled or a button is pushed. 2. Place the vibrating toy against the child's hand. 3. Observe their curiosity as they feel the steady buzzing sensation.

1. Tape squares of different materials (tinfoil, felt, cardboard) to the floor in a line. 2. Encourage the child to crawl along the path. 3. Notice how they react to the "crinkle" of the foil versus the "soft" felt.

1. Mix corn flour with a little water to create "Oobleck" (a goop that is both solid and liquid). 2. Let the child punch the surface, then watch their hand sink in. 3. Show them how to scoop it up and watch it "melt" through their fingers.
Toy Photo (Col H): [Image: Bowl of white corn flour goop]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Fill small plastic bottles with different amounts of water. 2. Shake the bottles to show how the sound changes based on the water level. 3. Let the child shake them to feel the weight shift and hear the splashing.
1. Use a very soft makeup brush or a baby hairbrush. 2. Gently "paint" the child’s hand or foot with the dry bristles. 3. Describe the sensation as "tickly" or "soft" to build sensory vocabulary.
Tools (Column E): Soft baby brush or makeup brush

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place small, soft pieces of food (like steamed carrots) on a high-chair tray. 2. Show the child how to pick up one piece using their thumb and forefinger. 3. Encourage them to bring the food to their mouth independently.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child picking up a small snack]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Use a small, open cup with a tiny amount of water. 2. Guide the child's hands to hold both sides of the cup. 3. Help them tip it slowly to take a small sip without spilling.
1. At the end of play, bring a large bin to the center of the room. 2. Pick up a toy and say "In the box!". 3. Hand a toy to the child and guide them to drop it into the bin.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child putting a doll in a box]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Loosen the heel of the child's sock slightly. 2. Show them how to grab the toe part of the sock. 3. Encourage them to pull the sock all the way off their foot.
1. Stand the child at the sink using a secure step stool. 2. Apply a small drop of mild soap to their hands. 3. Help them rub their palms together and rinse under the water.

1. Apply a smear of child-safe toothpaste to a small brush. 2. Let the child hold the handle while you guide the bristles over their teeth. 3. Allow them to "brush" on their own for a few seconds to build familiarity.

1. Provide a bowl of thick food (like yogurt or oatmeal) that stays on a spoon. 2. Scoop a small amount and hand the spoon to the child. 3. Guide their hand to their mouth to help them learn the scooping motion.
1. Place a soft, loose hat on the child's head while looking in a mirror. 2. Show them how to grab the brim and pull it off. 3. Encourage them to try and "plop" the hat back onto their head.
1. Hold out a shirt with a wide neck opening. 2. Encourage the child to push their arms through the sleeve holes. 3. Praise their effort as they help pull the garment down over their tummy.
1. After washing hands, hand a small, soft towel to the child. 2. Show them how to rub the towel over their wet hands. 3. Encourage them to "pat-pat" their skin until the water is gone.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child rubbing hands with a towel]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Identify a low, open shelf where a specific toy belongs. 2. Hand the toy to the child and point to the shelf. 3. Guide them to walk over and place the toy neatly in its "home."
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a toy on a shelf]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a few dry crackers on a lightweight, non-slip plastic plate. 2. Have the child hold the plate with both hands. 3. Encourage them to walk a short distance to the table without dropping the crackers.
1. Provide a child-safe water bottle with a straw or spout. 2. Show them how to flip the lid or position the straw. 3. Encourage them to hold the bottle and drink independently throughout the day.
1. Place a sturdy, child-sized chair near the child. 2. Show them how to turn around and back up toward the seat. 3. Assist them in lowering themselves safely into the chair to sit.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child sitting down in a small chair]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. After a nap, lay the child's small blanket flat on the floor. 2. Show them how to take two corners and bring them to the middle. 3. Encourage them to "smooth" the blanket with their hands.
1. Designate a specific spot or mat near the door for shoes. 2. Hand the child their shoes after coming inside. 3. Encourage them to bend down and place the shoes neatly on the designated spot.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing shoes on a mat]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a small piece of clean laundry (like a sock). 2. Point to the laundry basket. 3. Encourage them to walk over and drop the item into the basket to "help" with chores.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child dropping a sock in a basket]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. After a meal, show the child your empty spoon. 2. Guide them to a low plastic basin or the kitchen sink. 3. Encourage them to drop their used spoon into the basin to signal the end of the meal.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child putting a spoon in a tub]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a small, safe piece of trash (like a paper scrap). 2. Point to a small, open wastebasket. 3. Encourage them to drop the paper inside and say "All gone!".
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child dropping paper in a bin]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Place a very light item (like a plush toy) in a small tote bag. 2. Hand the handle of the bag to the child. 3. Encourage them to carry the bag while walking from one room to another.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child walking with a small bag]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Hand the child a sturdy board book. 2. Point to a low, reachable shelf. 3. Guide them to slide the book onto the shelf alongside others.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing a book on a shelf]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Give the child a small, damp microfiber cloth. 2. Demonstrate a circular wiping motion on a low table. 3. Encourage them to "clean up" their play surface.
1. Point to scattered toys on the floor. 2. Hand one toy to the child and gesture toward the box. 3. Celebrate every toy they successfully put inside the container.
1. Open a low, safe drawer (e.g., in a play kitchen). 2. Show the child how to place their palms flat on the front. 3. Encourage them to push until the drawer clicks shut.
1. After drinking, guide the child to hold their cup with both hands. 2. Point to a flat, clear spot on the table. 3. Encourage them to set the cup down gently without tipping it over.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child placing cup on a table]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Drop a clean washcloth or napkin on the floor. 2. Ask the child "Can you get that?". 3. Encourage them to bend their knees, pick up the cloth, and hand it to you.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child bending to pick up cloth]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Provide an easy-to-open lunch box with a simple latch. 2. Show the child how to lift the clip. 3. Encourage them to pull the lid open to find a small treat or toy inside.
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child lifting a lunch box lid]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. During a meal, hand the child a clean paper or cloth napkin. 2. Show them how to hold it in their lap or hand. 3. Encourage them to use it to "pat" their mouth after eating.

1. When entering the house, point to a specific shoe rack or mat. 2. Assist the child in taking off their shoes. 3. Encourage them to carry the shoes over and set them down in the designated "shoe home".
Activity Photo (Col I): [Image: Child setting shoes on a mat]

Description (Detailed Steps): 1. Lay a small square washcloth flat. 2. Show the child how to bring two corners together to make a rectangle. 3. Help them press down on the fold with their palm to make it "neat".
